result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Both answers advise against approving every filing, keep a log or digest with a way to move files back, and send ambiguous cases to a review step. B makes up figures: '10 to 15 items a week', a 5% tripwire and a 5-minute digest. It also adds extras like hash-based duplicate checks and per-client fallback modes. A avoids made-up numbers and gives its cofounder reply as direct advice, though its section on turning corrections into rules runs a bit long. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): B names the specific uncertain cases that should stop and ask (unknown sender, two matching clients, unreadable PDF, new client). Its daily digest gives each filing its own move-back control. It also avoids made-up volume estimates. A is a little shorter, but it predicts '10 to 15 items a week' without basis, adds extras like hash checks and tripwire thresholds, and is less clear about which cases need approval.
